edits.note: Round 1. Verified rather than edited. Will's note was an uncertain recollection ('I think') of a winter osprey sighting at the creek. content/research/winter-birding-northern-neck.md and the voice-feedback-log's 2026-08-08 entry (item 3, northern-neck-in-fall-from-dc correction) both establish, from sourced research, that Chesapeake-region ospreys migrate south starting in August, most depart by September, and reach Central/South America by mid-October, not returning until spring. That makes ospreys essentially absent from Hull Creek in winter, which matches this post's existing framing ('gone by October,' the water going quiet, the season built around swans/eagles/ducks/geese instead). Per instructions, this note is resolved by confirming that existing framing is correct and by deliberately not adding any invented winter-osprey sighting, rather than by changing post text. No wording in the post was altered for this note.
